source.title: The Perception-Physics Paradox: Probing Scientific Alignment with TC-Bench
source.authors: Ding-Ling Yao; Andrea Polesello; Adeel Pervez; C. Muller; Francesco Locatello

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether frozen vision representations preserve physical state information, not whether representations from different models become more similar with scale or capability. Its discussion distinguishes model-to-model representation alignment from grounding representations in physical reality.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own physical-state probes and within-model latent-geometry diagnostics. These concern a related but different construct from the listed convergence versions, so rows are marked versions ["none"] and summarized under fits_no_version. References to model-to-model alignment work are not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study probes frozen vision foundation models for linear recoverability of cyclone physical state (pressure, its temporal change, pressure–wind coupling) and within-model latent geometry. It never compares representations between models, across seeds, across modalities, or across scale, and no mapping between models is attempted. Platonic Representation Hypothesis and relative-representation work are cited only in related work, where the authors contrast model-to-model alignment with grounding in physics. The abstract's line that alignment does not arise from scaling alone has no scale sweep behind it.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that frozen VFMs appear perceptually robust yet lose physically meaningful latent resolution in intense cyclone regimes. They say standard OOD tests miss this, and they contrast scientific alignment with model-to-model representation alignment.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not apply the model-to-model similarity methods of the cited representation-alignment work; it probes representations against physical variables and constraints.

fits_no_version.finding: All evaluated frozen VFMs (DINOv2/v3, CLIP, SigLIP/2, MAE, plus video models) lose linear recoverability of cyclone pressure, dynamic coherence and pressure–wind consistency in the intense regime. DINOv3-base latent effective dimensionality drops about 60% there. A ResNet-18 trained from scratch shows the signal is still in the images.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Frozen VFMs share a common regime-dependent collapse along physically meaningful axes, i.e. similar blind spots across model families, even with strong perceptual or OOD performance.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR 306, 2026)
record.problems: No direct model-to-model similarity or scale sweep is reported. Several main figures provide qualitative trends without numerical values in the text; uncertainty is reported for some appendix probe results but not for the main geometry comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results were retained: other reported checks and plots concern the same physical-state probing question or provide supporting visualizations, not model-to-model convergence.

untested.parts: No comparison of representations between independently trained models, and no sweep over size or capability.
No comparison of models trained from different seeds.
No stitching, linear mapping or relative-representation transfer between models.
No cross-model comparison of features or circuits.
No test of how the similarity metric or input data change measured inter-model convergence.
No measurement of the degree, plateau or causes of inter-model alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The record's appendix results (Table 4 nonlinear probes; Table 5 video models, e.g. V-JEPA2 0.235 vs 0.334) are omitted. That omission does not matter for the versions, since none bear on convergence. The same degradation appearing across many model families is consistent with shared failure modes, but it is not a measure of representational similarity.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of independently trained models' representations across model size or capability.
No measurement of image-caption representation alignment.
No comparison of models trained from different seeds.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test between models.
No comparison of recurring features or circuits across models.
No test of how choices of similarity metric or input data affect measured model-to-model convergence.
No test of whether model-to-model alignment plateaus or is explained by shared data or objectives.

rows.subject: all evaluated VFMs
rows.operation_detail: Linear regression probe of minimum central pressure from CLS representations
rows.measure: Normalized static fidelity error ξstat; ξstat = 1.0 is a naive mean estimator
rows.value: intense regime has sharply higher median error and more catastrophic outliers (ξstat > 1.0); figure-only
rows.note: The text reports this qualitative degradation across all evaluated model families; this is physical-state recoverability, not inter-model similarity.
rows.check: Measures physical-state recoverability, not inter-model similarity. State refers to the paper's own regime-degradation finding, not to any claim version.

rows.subject: all evaluated VFMs
rows.operation_detail: Finite-difference test of decoded latent displacement against physical pressure evolution

conditions.value: moderate versus intense; catastrophic regime Pc < 920 hPa

rows.baseline: moderate regime, where the gap is described as stable; numeric value not stated
rows.value: gap increases sharply below the 980 hPa threshold and has a pronounced spike for Pc < 920 hPa; figure-only
rows.note: Reports latent-to-physical dynamical alignment, not alignment between models.
rows.check: Latent-to-physical dynamic coherence, not model-to-model alignment.

rows.subject: all evaluated VFMs
rows.operation_detail: Linear recovery of pressure and wind followed by a pressure–wind constraint check
rows.note: The paper reports these across models as regime-level results; they measure physical constraint preservation, not model-to-model convergence.
rows.check: Physical constraint preservation, not convergence. Clear degradation (about 20% to about 55%) reads as observed rather than partial for the paper's own finding. Irrelevant to the versions either way.

rows.subject: DINOv3-base
rows.operation_detail: Participation ratio of within-pressure-bin feature covariance
rows.measure: Effective dimensionality of within-bin feature covariance
rows.value: Intense regime shows an approximately 60% reduction
rows.note: A within-model geometry diagnostic; the paper attributes the reduction to concentration of variation into fewer latent directions.
rows.check: Within-model geometry diagnostic for DINOv3-base only.

rows.value: Intense regime shows decreased feature spread; numerical amount not stated
